name: Three Parallel Rivers of Yunnan Protected Areas
blurb: Lichen, monkeys, takin and snow leopards in the gorges of the Hengduan range.

tip.title: Strip the old-growth lichen
tip.text: The snub-nosed monkey lives mostly on tree lichen. Set Tree lichen to -80% and watch the monkey and musk deer, then the snow leopard and dhole.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Three Parallel Rivers of Yunnan Protected Areas

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.name: Sunlight and altitude
nodes.desc: Strong high-altitude light drives growth in meadows and forests between the gorges and the snowline.

nodes.name: Snowmelt and glacier water
nodes.desc: Melt from peaks such as Meili Xue Shan feeds the meadows and the headwaters of the Yangtze, Mekong and Salween.

nodes.name: Summer monsoon rain
nodes.desc: Rain from the south-west monsoon is very heavy in the western gorges and far lighter in the upper Yangtze valleys.

nodes.name: Mountain soil and litter
nodes.desc: Forest litter and meadow soil hold the nutrients that rhododendron, bamboo and conifers draw on.

nodes.name: Decomposers
nodes.desc: Fungi and bacteria break down dead plants, lichen and animals, returning nutrients to the soil.

nodes.name: Rhododendron
nodes.desc: The region has hundreds of rhododendron kinds; they form shrub and forest layers. Snub-nosed monkeys feed on their nectar in spring.

nodes.name: Tree lichen
nodes.desc: Hanging lichens on old conifers are the main year-round food of the black snub-nosed monkey.

nodes.name: Bamboo
nodes.desc: Understory bamboo thickets give cover and food, eaten by monkeys, takin and bears.

nodes.name: Fir and conifer forest
nodes.desc: Conifer forest covers the high slopes where the monkeys live and gives seeds, shade and winter shelter.

nodes.name: Alpine meadow flowers
nodes.desc: Alpine meadows above the treeline are rich in primulas, gentians and grasses that grazers and small mammals eat.

nodes.name: Black snub-nosed monkey
nodes.desc: Endemic to northwest Yunnan and neighbouring Tibet. It lives higher than any other non-human primate and lives mostly on lichen.

nodes.name: Takin
nodes.desc: Stocky goat-antelope that browses leaves, bamboo shoots and flowers, moving down to forest in winter.

nodes.name: Blue sheep
nodes.desc: A mountain grazer of grass, switching to forbs and shrubs when grass is scarce. A favoured prey of the snow leopard.

nodes.name: Yak
nodes.desc: Herded yaks graze the alpine pastures and are sometimes taken by snow leopards and scavenged when they die.

nodes.name: Black musk deer
nodes.desc: Small, secretive deer of high forest that feeds on plants and lichen. Preyed on by dholes and other carnivores.

nodes.name: Moupin pika
nodes.desc: Colonial burrower of rocky ground under rhododendron and bamboo that stores haypiles of plants.

nodes.name: South China field mouse
nodes.desc: A well-recorded forest rodent of the Hengduan mountains and a staple small prey for carnivores.

nodes.name: Asian black bear
nodes.desc: Omnivore of nuts, seeds, bamboo shoots, insects and carrion; it also kills ungulates such as takin.

nodes.name: Yellow-throated marten
nodes.desc: Agile forest hunter of small mammals and birds, hunting from the canopy to the ground.

nodes.name: Large-billed crow
nodes.desc: Widespread, highly recorded scavenger and generalist that cleans up carcasses on the slopes.

nodes.name: Snow leopard
nodes.desc: Top predator of the high cliffs and meadows; hunts blue sheep and musk deer plus pikas, marmots and voles.

nodes.name: Dhole
nodes.desc: Pack-hunting wild dog recorded in Baima Xueshan; hunts deer including musk deer, plus rodents.
